div.head: I Atr 1.2
div.ab: Gif se hlaford sæcge, þæt him naðer ne burste ne að ne ordal, syððan þæt gemot wæs æt Bromdune, nime se hlaford him twegen getreowe þegenas innan þam hundrede, ⁊ swerian, þæt him næfre að ne burste, ne he þeofgyld ne gulde — butan he þone gerefan hæbbe, þe þæs wyrðe sy, þe þæt don mæge.

Gyf se hlaford sæcge, þæt him naðor ne burste ne að ne ordal, syððan þæt gemot wæs æt Bromdune, nime se hlaford him twegen getreowa ðegenas innan ðam hundrede, ⁊ swerian, þæt him næfre að ne burste, ne he ðeofgyld ne gulde — buton he ðone gerefan hæbbe, ðe ðæs wyrðe sy, þe þæt don mæge.

Si dominus eius dicat, quod neutrum ei fregit uel aþ uel ordal, postquam concilium fuit apud Brundonam, assumat idem dominus sibi duos credibiles tainos in ipso hundreto et iuret, quod numquam iusiurandum (iuramentum) fregit nec furigildum persoluit — nisi talem prepositum habeat, qui dignus eo sit, ut hoc facere possit.

Gyf se hlaford sæcge þæt him naðor ne burste ne að ne ordal syððan þæt gemot wæs æt Bromdune, nime se hlaford him twegen getreowa ðegenas innan ðam hundrede ⁊ swerian þæt him næfre að ne burste ne he ðeofgyld ne gulde—buton he ðone gerefan hæbbe ðe ðæs wyrðe sy þe þæt don mæge.

Wenn der Herr [desselben freilich] behauptet, dass jenem, seitdem der [Reichs]tag zu ‘Bromdun’ war, weder Eid noch Ordal fehlgeschlagen sei, so wähle sich der Herr zwei vertrauenswürdige Thegnas innerhalb dieser [einen] Hundertschaft, und [diese drei] sollen schwören, ‘dass jenem nie weder Eid fehlschlug, noch er Diebesbusse bezahlen musste’ — es sei denn, der [Herr] habe einen solchen Amtmann, der dazu berechtigt ist, dass er dies thun dürfe [statt des Gutsherrn].

But if his lord asserts that neither oath nor ordeal has failed him since the assembly at ‘Bromdun’, let the lord choose two trustworthy thegns within that [one] hundred, and [these three] are to swear ‘that neither oath ever failed him nor did he have to pay theft-compensation’ — unless [the lord] has a reeve who is entitled to do this [in place of the lord].

If his lord asserts that he (the accused) has failed neither in oath nor in ordeal since the assembly was held at Bromdun, he (the lord) shall choose two trustworthy thegns within the hundred, and they shall swear that neither has his oath ever failed nor has he been convicted of stealing—unless the lord have a reeve who is qualified to discharge this duty.
div.note: H lacks ‘ne ordal’ after ‘að ne burste’; Liebermann supplies it from II Cn 30.1. Liebermann compares III Atr 4.

Die engere Bed. ‘Reichstag’ folgt nur aus Analogie; Cnut setzt statt dieser Epoche: ‘Winchester’-Reichstag
The narrower meaning ‘national assembly’ follows only from analogy; for this date Cnut substitutes: the ‘Winchester’ assembly

Dass der Reichstag unter Æthelred II. stattfand, folgt nur aus Analogie; s. Witan 10; Kemble's (Saxons II 257) Datierung vor 997 hängt ab von seinem Datum 997 für III Atr.—Parker Early Oxford 394 hält für möglich sowohl Brumdun (Urk. a. 1035 Ke 1322), jetzt Brumdon in Dorset, wie Bromden (Bi 377. 689. Ke 780), im Domesday I 49b Brondene. Letzteres schliess ich wegen des -e- aus. Der Index zum Domesday kennt Brumduna in Essex. Wegen des -l- ausgeschlossen scheint mir Brumetone I 86b, jetzt Brompton regis in Somerset

That the assembly took place under Æthelred II follows only from analogy; see Witan 10; Kemble’s (Saxons II 257) dating before 997 depends on his date of 997 for III Atr.—Parker Early Oxford 394 considers possible both Brumdun (charter a. 1035 Ke 1322), now Brumdon in Dorset, and Bromden (Bi 377. 689. Ke 780), in Domesday I 49b Brondene. The latter I exclude because of the -e-. The index to Domesday records a Brumduna in Essex. Brumetone I 86b, now Brompton regis in Somerset, seems to me excluded because of the -l-

Über diese Erschwerung durch örtlich begrenzten Kreis der Mitschwörer s. Eideshelfer 10—12. Vielleicht hat Thegn (s. d. Gl 8) hier nur die Bed. ‘vollfreier Grundbesitzer’, nicht bloss enger ‘Adliger von 1200 Schilling Wergeld’.—Die Wahl der Helfer verbleibt dem Herrn ausdrücklich

On this aggravation through a locally restricted circle of co-swearers see Eideshelfer 10—12. Perhaps thegn (see that word in Gl 8) here has only the meaning ‘fully free landowner’, and not merely the narrower ‘noble with a wergild of 1200 shillings’.—The choice of the helpers expressly remains with the lord
Falls die Worte ne ordal absichtlich im Original fehlen, sind sie doch hinzuzudenken aus 2 Zeilen vorher oder aus weiterer Bed. von ‘Eid’ (s. d. Gl 1a), die Ordal mitumfassen kann

If the words ne ordal are deliberately absent from the original, they are nevertheless to be understood, either from 2 lines before or from the wider meaning of ‘oath’ (see that word in Gl 1a), which can include ordeal
Vgl. Gl Vogt 3d. 13; Herrschaftsgut 5; Adelsbeamter 4f. 8. Der Adlige kann auch im Klageeid (s. d. Gl 5c) sich vertreten lassen
Cf. Gl Vogt 3d. 13; Herrschaftsgut 5; Adelsbeamter 4f. 8. The noble may also be represented in the oath of accusation (see that word in Gl 5c)
Er musste wohl Vollfreier sein wie die zwei eben geforderten Helfer und der Vertreter im Klageeid
He probably had to be a fully free man, like the two helpers just required and the representative in the oath of accusation

Q has apud Brundonam. The identification is uncertain as there are many places in England with similar names. Liebermann suggests as possible Brumdun (see Kemble, 1322), now Brumdon in Dorset (cf. Parker, Early Oxford, p. 394), and Brumduna [Branduna], now Brundon in Essex (see DB. ii. 90 and 90 b)
